predictions.title: Per-tenant capability-attestation logs ship as MCP framework default by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 9 capability-attestation convergence forces signed per-tenant capability-attestation logs out of the Anthropic-specific Project Glasswing posture and into the default control-plane primitive shipped by every major MCP-server framework and hyperscaler-managed agentic-AI runtime. The catalysts that land in a single weekend cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: a Saturday arxiv preprint (2605.05933) by MIT CSAIL, ETH Zurich, and Anthropic provides a formal-verification framework for per-tenant capability attestation over MCP tool-call graphs and proves a no-cross-tenant-information-leakage property under the gating composition rule, giving downstream framework maintainers a citable safety theorem rather than a hand-waved design pattern; Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server threat-detection module now quarantines 24 percent of net-new MCP servers seen on Defender-protected estates within the first 30 minutes of provisioning, up from 19 percent the day before, demonstrating that the unattested control-plane surface is the operational attack surface; Cisco-Astrix's MCP-server identity gateway (co-branded with Defender XDR plus the Microsoft Agent 365 audit ledger) reaches 740 enterprise-tenant deployments inside its first 48 hours, signalling that the demand-side has moved past pilots; Sysdig Threat Research's weekend addendum reports median time-from-MCP-server-provisioning to first credential-extraction-attempt has fallen to 19 minutes on unprotected estates versus 4.3 hours on Defender-protected tenants, putting a measurable cost on the absence of attestation; and the Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog plus AWS Bedrock Agent Registry plus Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center weekend updates extend signed-skill-provenance and reciprocity-attestation surface across all three hyperscaler-managed agentic runtimes within 48 hours of the Anthropic and OpenAI registry launches. The structural force is that once a peer-reviewed leakage-freedom proof exists for the gating composition rule, framework maintainers can cite the theorem rather than ship bespoke audit logic, and the Defender plus Sysdig telemetry numbers convert the question from policy to procurement. The most likely shape is a per-tenant attestation-log primitive added as a first-class object in the modelcontextprotocol reference server, the FastMCP Python framework, the LangChain MCP adapter, the LlamaIndex MCP toolkit, and the three hyperscaler agent registries, with default schemas for capability scope, tenant identity, gating-rule composition trace, and a verifiable-event chain that holds up to the audit-trail review Simon Willison flagged Saturday. Sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt it first because the Mythos-class capability gating is already a procurement gate. Bear case is a competing framework refusing the composition rule and forking the schema; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signed per-tenant attestation logs as the documented default across the cohort.

reasoning.given: Defender quarantines 24% of new MCP servers; Sysdig logs 19-min credential extraction unprotected.
reasoning.so_that: FastMCP, LangChain, LlamaIndex MCP toolkits + three hyperscaler registries ship per-tenant attestation logs by default.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; sovereign-cloud + FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt first.
reasoning.plain_language: Researchers proved a way to log AI-agent permissions safely across tenants, so the main agent toolkits will copy that logging by default.

predictions.summary: A May 9 MIT CSAIL + ETH Zurich + Anthropic arxiv paper proves no-cross-tenant-leakage for per-tenant MCP capability gating, while Defender quarantines 24% of new MCP servers and Sysdig logs 19-min credential extraction. By Q4 2026 per-tenant attestation logs ship as MCP framework default.

predictions.title: AI-accelerator S-1s ship per-counterparty risk-factor table by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the May 9 accelerator-IPO cohort weekend update — Tenstorrent's confidential S-1 draft filed under the JOBS Act EGC framework late Friday with public-filing windows opening early August and Hyundai Motor Group plus Samsung Foundry retaining co-anchor positions on the $3.4B fully-closed bridge round, SambaNova naming J.P. Morgan and Citi as joint lead bookrunners alongside Goldman Sachs for an S-1 confidential submission targeted late June at a $7-9B fully-diluted valuation range, Groq trailing 30-60 days behind pending sovereign-cloud Saudi-Arabia commitment closure, plus Bernstein's Saturday Market-Perform initiation on Cerebras CBRS at $172 citing Saudi Aramco Digital MoU dependency as the top single-counterparty concentration risk against the Morgan Stanley / Goldman / Citi Buy-rated $165-$185 cohort and the Cerebras CFO Saturday confirmation of the October 28 2026 180-day lock-up with no early-release waiver for OpenAI's $1B warrant package — combined with the SEC Corp Fin Saturday clarifying footnote treating the May 8 sample comment letter as generally applicable guidance and the same staff's standing line of inquiry on customer-concentration footnotes across the Mag-7 cohort, force the next-wave AI-accelerator S-1 cohort to standardize a single-counterparty risk-factor exhibit — a per-customer table naming counterparty, percentage-of-revenue or backlog band, contract tenor, take-or-pay language, and any sovereign-jurisdiction or export-control overlay — as the operative S-1 format rather than narrative-only disclosure. The forcing function is that once sell-side initiation on a freshly-listed comparable anchors a Market-Perform call on single-counterparty concentration, subsequent S-1 underwriters cannot let narrative-only language stand without inviting a Corp Fin comment-letter cycle that pushes the deal calendar. The likely shape is a tabular exhibit in Tenstorrent's August public-filing window, mirrored by SambaNova late June and Groq inside the same window. Bear case is a separate concept release deferring the format to 10-K disclosure; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the standardized exhibit across the cohort.

predictions.title: Allied agentic-AI CVE blocklist hardens into procurement gate by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the NHS England agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE blocklist published Saturday — naming Ni8mare (n8n CVE-2026-21858), LangGraph CVE-2026-44012, LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188, CrewAI CVE-2026-44352, and Haystack CVE-2026-44391 as disallowed pre-patch versions on NHS-tenant deployments — combined with Mistral's DGFiP central-tax-administration Workflows selection (cited control-plane separation + sovereign-cloud execution-worker shape over LangGraph self-hosted plus the Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 registry) and the South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB weekend extensions of the Singapore IMDA / Japan AISI cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter, will harden into a named-CVE-pegged sovereign-procurement gate adopted across at least four allied public-sector procurement regimes (UK NHS + France DGFiP + at least one Indo-Pacific signatory + one EU member-state framework agreement). The forcing function is that NHS England has now demonstrated a publishable per-CVE blocklist tied to a federal-civilian KEV-mirroring deadline (CISA May 21), Mistral has demonstrated that sovereign-cloud control-plane separation wins a flagship central-government estate against the LangGraph self-hosted alternative explicitly named on that blocklist, and the Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter now binds AISI-administered cyber-eval results as the operative threshold across the allied cohort. Once a UK frontline NHS trust + a French central-tax-administration estate publish concordant CVE-pegged tenancy terms and Anthropic's per-tenant attestation-log primitive (praised by Simon Willison Saturday as the first vendor-side governance shape that holds up to sustained audit-trail review) becomes the canonical compliance evidence, the gate composes from voluntary blocklist into procurement-mandate language. The most likely shape is a four-jurisdiction CVE-pegged annex (UK + France + Singapore-or-Japan + Germany-or-Netherlands BSI-equivalent) treating per-CVE remediation status plus per-tenant Mythos-class capability attestation as paired procurement-eligibility evidence, with the operative review cadence aligned to the AISI cyber-eval reciprocity 120-day placement window. Bear case is that CISA fast-tracks an agentic-AI workflow KEV-bundle Binding Operational Directive that pre-empts the allied perimeter; absent that, Q4 2026 lands the named-CVE procurement gate.

reasoning.because: NHS England publishes named-CVE agentic-AI blocklist alongside DGFiP Mistral Workflows selection.
reasoning.given: Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter widens to South Korea PIPC and New Zealand GCSB the same weekend.
reasoning.so_that: Allied public-sector procurement adopts named-CVE-pegged tenancy plus per-tenant attestation as eligibility.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; four jurisdictions; CISA KEV-mirroring cadence.
reasoning.plain_language: Britain's NHS banned five risky AI tools by name; France picked a sovereign one, and allies will copy that buying rule.

predictions.summary: NHS England's named-CVE agentic-AI blocklist plus Mistral's DGFiP central-tax-administration win, combined with the South Korea and New Zealand reciprocity-perimeter extensions, harden allied public-sector procurement around CVE-pegged tenancy and per-tenant attestation evidence by Q4 2026.
